title: Building the Machines Behind the AI Boom
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

ASML has broken ground on BIC North, a manufacturing campus near its Veldhoven headquarters, signaling confidence that artificial-intelligence investment will sustain demand for advanced semiconductor equipment. The 35-hectare site, located near Eindhoven Airport, will include offices, logistics infrastructure and cleanrooms for assembling ASML’s lithography systems. Its first phase is scheduled for completion in 2029, while the campus could eventually accommodate 20,000 workers.

Central to the expansion is a “Flow Factory,” intended to increase manufacturing capacity and improve how complex machines move through assembly. ASML’s extreme-ultraviolet lithography tools are essential for producing leading-edge processors and memory chips. Customers including TSMC, Samsung, Intel and Micron depend on these systems to manufacture smaller, faster and more energy-efficient semiconductors. Nearly all of ASML’s EUV capacity is reportedly booked through 2027, demonstrating how rapidly AI infrastructure is absorbing chipmaking capacity.

The project also strengthens the Eindhoven region’s position as a European technology cluster. Semiconductor supply chains depend on engineering talent, precision suppliers, transport links and public infrastructure; concentrating those capabilities around ASML can accelerate production but also creates regional dependencies.

For Europe, the investment offers a counterpoint to industrial contraction elsewhere and reinforces technological sovereignty in critical industries. For ASML, however, execution will be demanding. The company must recruit skilled workers, coordinate thousands of suppliers and expand without compromising the precision or reliability of machines that cost hundreds of millions of euros. BIC North is therefore more than a real-estate project: it is a long-term bet that AI-driven semiconductor demand will remain durable. (Reuters)
